title: Causal Chain Intervention: Improving Tool Documentation Quality as a Leverage Point for AI Attack Capability

original_idea.body:
# Causal Chain Intervention: Improving Tool Documentation Quality as a Leverage Point for AI Attack Capability

**Problem:** AI agents often fail at tool invocation steps (wrong parameters, misunderstood output) rather than at reasoning steps. If tool documentation quality is a causal bottleneck, improving it would directly advance AI offensive capability — which is important to understand for dual-use risk assessment.

**Direction:** Take 5 standard security tools (nmap, gobuster, sqlmap, netcat, john). Create two versions of documentation: (A) standard man page / default help text, (B) AI-optimized documentation with explicit input/output format, common failure modes, and example completions. Run AI agents on 10 CTF challenges with each documentation version. Measure the performance delta attributable to documentation quality.

**Why it matters:** If documentation quality is a major bottleneck, then the gap between current AI capability and full chain completion may be much smaller than it appears — improvable with simple engineering, not fundamental capability advances. This is critical for accurate threat forecasting.

**Relevant context:** Context relay paper (NDSS 2026) addressed context management for long-running agents. Pentest-AI GitHub (2026) documented 150+ security tools with explicit formatting. AISI found standard tools increasingly replacing custom toolkits. AWS Security Agent used specialized tool documentation for each sub-agent.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Measures AI offensive capability, informing defensive research. Connection to catastrophic risk reduction is plausible but indirect.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Requires access to LLM APIs, security infrastructure, and sophisticated evaluation design. Likely beyond beginner capability.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Requires experimental isolation of confounds; complex to design and execute cleanly in 30 hours.
